prerequisites.title: Admin access to the Kintone domain
prerequisites.detail: Clients are registered on the User & System Administration page of a Kintone domain.

prerequisites.title: Your own client ID and secret
prerequisites.detail: Composio has no managed app for Kintone REST, so you must supply your own.

steps.title: Open the OAuth settings in Kintone
steps.detail: Log in, click the gear icon, open User & System Administration, then OAuth.
steps.done_when: The Add OAuth Client button is visible.

steps.title: Copy the redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard for the Kintone REST auth config.

steps.title: Add the OAuth client
steps.detail: Enter a client name (required) and the redirect endpoint (required), then click Save.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are generated.

steps.title: Enable users for the client
steps.detail: Click Configure users next to the client and check each user who may connect.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Use Composio's API to create a custom auth config for kintone_rest with the client ID and secret, and the scopes needed.

steps.title: Test a connection
steps.detail: Connect a test user, log in to Kintone and approve the request.

traps.title: New users are disabled by default
traps.detail: A new client has no enabled users, and each newly created Kintone user is unchecked until an admin enables them.

traps.title: IP restrictions block OAuth clients
traps.detail: On domains with IP restrictions, the OAuth client's IP must be allowlisted.

traps.title: Short-lived tokens and codes
traps.detail: Access tokens last 1 hour and authorization codes 10 minutes. Refresh tokens do not expire.

traps.title: Client and token limits
traps.detail: Up to 20 OAuth clients can be registered, and up to 10 refresh tokens per client per user.

blockers.symptom: Users cannot authorize or the API returns errors
blockers.what_it_means: The user may not be enabled for the client, or the scope does not cover the API.
blockers.what_to_do: Check Configure users and request the right scopes, space separated.
blockers.agent_can_help: Check the scope list against the APIs your agent calls.
